newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China paroles jailed Hong Kong newspaper reporter.
newsitem.headline: China paroles jailed Hong Kong newspaper reporter.

text.p: HONG KONG, Jan 25 - A Hong Kong newspaper journalist who was paroled by China on Saturday after serving three years of a 12-year prison term for stealing state secrets returned to the British colony and described his release as a surprise.

Xi Yang, a former reporter for Hong Kong's Chinese-language Ming Pao newspaper, was released with 157 days to go before the colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1. He was greeted on arrival in the colonly by colleagues who presented him with a large cake.
"I was surprised by the release. My health and spirits are fine," Xi said in a statement read out by the paper's Group Chief editor Kao Hsin-chiang.
"We would like to thank the Chinese government and the Hong Kong government for their concern."
A tired-looking Xi sat quietly, visibly overcome with emotion and occasionally wiping his face.
His sister read out a letter from Xi's father in Beijing expressing the family's joy and relief.
"Xi Yang's parole was a surprise for me and I am extremely happy," his father, Xi Linsheng, said in the note.
"His early release is our family's dream," the note said. It expressed the Xi family's "heartfelt thanks to friends, Hong Kong people and those who cared for Xi Yang".
China's official news agency Xinhua said Xi was released on parole because he "showed signs of repentance".
Xi's collegues said they had been told his health had deteriorated while he was in prison.

He was released early on Saturday morning and visited his family in Beijing before flying to Hong Kong. Xi said he was too tired to think about his future and had not decided whether to return to journalism.
China jailed Xi for 12 years in March 1994 on charges of stealing state secrets about internal policies on interest rates nnd gold.
The severity of the sentence shocked Hong Kong reporters, already pessimistic about the prospects for a free press after the handover and triggered protests in the British colony.
"I am delighted at the news that Mr Xi Yang has been released from prison and is now back in Hong Kong," the colony's governor, Chris Patten, said.

"His case has caused great anxiety and concern to his family, his colleagues and the whole community. His release is very good news for Hong Kong as we approach the Chinese New Year (on February 7)," Patten added.

Pro-democracy activists have staged protests over the past week objecting to China's plans to dilute Hong Kong's civil liberties laws. China insists the alterations would not weaken human rights protections in the territory after the handover.
